claims.text: Ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder initially forms a simple BCC solid solution.
SPS at 1000 °C produces a dense MgAlTiVFeCo microstructure.
SPS at 1000 °C produces uniformly distributed barrier oxide phases.
The proposed barrier phases include AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3.
The dense microstructure and barrier oxide phases improve corrosion resistance relative to lower-temperature SPS samples.
The dense microstructure and barrier oxide phases improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to lower-temperature SPS samples.
High temperature and pressure during SPS enhance elemental diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion promotes nucleation and growth of a continuous passive film and barrier oxide phases.
The barrier phases impede chloride-ion penetration during corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
The barrier phases control oxygen diffusion during oxidation at 900 °C in air.
Oxygen-diffusion control produces parabolic oxidation kinetics.
Oxidation proceeds through two distinct growth regimes.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C will reach approximately 96.7% relative density and be denser than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C will reach approximately 1235.5 HV and be harder than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C will have a more positive corrosion potential than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C will have a lower corrosion current density and higher polarization resistance than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
Lower-temperature samples have poorer density, hardness, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance because they form less effective barrier phases.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient diffusion for proper densification and barrier-phase formation.
